correctness.rationale: Operational-time conditioning gives P(T>t)=E f_x(Lambda_t) for killed unit-rate symmetric walk; reflected Bessel heat kernels yield f_x(u)~x sqrt(2/pi)u^(−1/2) and a global bounded domination. The exact product Laplace transform of independent rates over intervals produces a stable triangular-array limit Lambda_t/B_t^(1/alpha)⇒Z_alpha because the largest normalized interval weight vanishes. A Mellin–beta bound on negative moments proves uniform integrability and the prefactor x sqrt(2) Gamma(1/(2alpha))/(alpha pi). Sum-integral clock inversion gives gamma=(1+alpha beta)/(2alpha(1+beta)), eta=delta(gamma−1/2), the full explicit positive constant and q-moment criterion q<gamma or q=gamma, eta<−1. The mean threshold alpha<1/(beta+2), with alpha=1/(beta+2), delta<−2, follows. Independent finite-stage spectral quadratures checked 3 parameter regimes with normalized survival ratios near 1.01; asymptotic proof rests on triangular arrays and negative moments, not finite simulations.
